matter_reference_date_basis: matter_reference_date field of candidates/matters/M020.json; exam session OCTOBER 2025. All provisions relied on are read in their form as consolidated after the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024, the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024 and the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024, all of which precede October 2025.
corpus_gaps: The corpus holds no Partition Act (No. 21 of 1977) and no rules or regulations made under the Notaries Ordinance, so nothing in the answer rests on partition-specific procedure; the analysis is confined to how a deed of partition, being a deed affecting immovable property, may be signed and attested.

No instrument in the corpus defines the geographical limits of the Colombo or Hambantota judicial zones, or lists which districts fall into which zone. That Tangalle lies outside the Colombo judicial zone is treated as a scenario fact, not as a corpus-derived fact.

Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 s.2 still refers to a Commissioner of a Court of Requests, an office abolished by later court-structure legislation that is not in this corpus. Only the District Judge limb of that section is relied on, and its present-day availability could not be confirmed from the corpus.
The corpus contains no provision on remote, audio-visual or electronic notarial attestation, so no such route was considered.

Stamp duty rates for a deed of partition are not in the corpus (the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 and the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 are present but the operative rate schedules were not consulted and are not needed for this question).

Verifier: the corpus does not settle whether a deed of partition of land held in common falls within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance; the section does not name partition, and Stamp Duty Act s.5(11) and Western Province Financial Statute s.106 treat a deed of partition as distinct from a transfer.

Verifier: the corpus carries the paragraphs inserted into section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance after rule (15), and the group forming rules (26) and (27), without rule numbers, so subsection-level citations into those groups cannot be confirmed from the corpus.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (22) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice
provisions.why_relevant: This is the territorial bar that creates the problem. The notary instructed holds a licence to practise in Colombo, so he cannot lawfully attest the signature of the co-owner who is in Tangalle by travelling there; any solution must work around this rule rather than through it.
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (22) of section 31 is part of the Ordinance as enacted in 1907 and was not touched by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts recorded against section 31. In force at October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (12) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
provisions.why_relevant: Fixes what a valid signing event requires: the executant and the witnesses must sign in the presence of the attesting notary and of one another. It is why the Tangalle co-owner cannot simply post her signature to Colombo, and why whichever notary takes her signature must be physically with her.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1907 rule; no amendment event recorded against it. In force at October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (25) Where any deed or instrument is executed or acknowledged before more than one notary- (a) the notary who first attests such deed or instrument shall comply with all the requirements of rule (20), and every other notary attesting such deed or instrument shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the aforesaid rule
provisions.why_relevant: The central enabling provision. It shows that one and the same deed may be executed before more than one notary, which allows the three Colombo parties to sign before the Colombo notary and the Tangalle party to sign before a notary licensed for the area in which she is, and it sets out how each notary attests and keeps a protocol.
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (25) was restructured by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011 s.3 and stands in the consolidated text relied on. In force well before October 2025.
provisions.verifier_note: Rule (25)(a) confirmed verbatim; paragraphs (b) and (c) of the same rule, on which the answer also relies, are added by the verifier as PROV-M020-902.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (2) In the case of any deed or instrument which is to be executed by two or more parties, both or all of whom, as the case may be, do not sign the deed or instrument at the same time and place-
provisions.why_relevant: Confirms that the Ordinance contemplates a multi-party deed whose parties do not all sign at the same time and place, and adjusts the operation of rules (6), (7), (18), (19), (20), (23) and (25) accordingly. Without it the staggered signing of the partition deed would have no statutory footing.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1907 section, no recorded amendment events. In force at October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
provisions.why_relevant: The deed of partition affects immovable property, so its validity depends on this section. It supplies both the strict requirement (every executant signs before a licensed notary and witnesses) and the opening for the alternative route, since it expressly allows signature by a person duly authorised by the executant.
provisions.temporal_note: Section 2 in its present form reflects amendments by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024, both in force before October 2025.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed, but section 2(1) is expressed by reference to a sale, purchase, transfer, assignment or mortgage and to agreements affecting land and does not name a deed of partition, and other corpus statutes (Stamp Duty Act s.5(11); Western Province Financial Statute s.106) treat a deed of partition of land held in common as distinct from a transfer, so the premise that the section governs this deed rests on characterisation rather than on the words of the section.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: a warrant authorizing him to practice as notary in the language in which he has passed the examination in conveyancing, within the judicial zone in which he resides
provisions.why_relevant: Supplies the content of the area referred to in rule (22): the warrant of an attorney-at-law notary is confined to the judicial zone in which he resides. It is what makes the Colombo licence a limit rather than a description.
provisions.temporal_note: Section 3 was replaced by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.2; the replacement text is quoted and was in force before October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every warrant issued to a notary under the provisions of section 3* or section 4* authorizing him to practice as a notary in any judicial division in which he resides, shall be deemed to authorize him to practice as a notary in the judicial zone in which he resides.
provisions.why_relevant: Widens an older division-based warrant to the whole judicial zone. It matters because it fixes the outer limit of the Colombo notary's authority: the zone, and no further. It does not reach a property or a party in Tangalle.
provisions.temporal_note: Inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.4; in force from 1976.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed, but section 4A operates only on a warrant issued under section 3 or section 4 for a judicial division, and section 3 as substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 already grants a zone warrant, so for a warrant issued at the matter date section 4A is of historic effect and is supporting rather than load-bearing.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (ii) where any such deed or instrument is not signed by all the parties thereto before the expiry of a period of three months from the date on which it is first signed by one of such parties
provisions.why_relevant: Puts a practical outer limit on the staggered-signing route: if the deed is not signed by all parties within three months of the first signature, the notary may be required to deliver the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands. It shapes the advice on timing.
provisions.temporal_note: Part of rule (27) as it stands in the consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against this sub-paragraph. In force at October 2025.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed, but the corpus text carries this group without the rule (26), rule (27) and paragraph (c) labels, and the provision imposes no three-month deadline: it obliges the notary to deliver the duplicate only if called upon by written notice, and the duplicate is returnable on demand within two years for completion of the deed.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (28) Where any deed or instrument other than a will or codicil shall be executed or acknowledged by two or more parties before more than one notary, the duplicate of such deed or instrument shall be delivered or transmitted by the notary who first attests such deed or instrument to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides
provisions.why_relevant: Allocates the duty to transmit the duplicate where two notaries attest the same deed, so the advice can say which notary carries the post-execution obligation and that the second notary need not duplicate it.
provisions.temporal_note: Consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against rule (28). In force at October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which such land shall be situated a copy thereof certified by him as correct, together with a list in duplicate in the Form F 1 in the Second Schedule
provisions.why_relevant: The land lies in a district other than that in which the Colombo notary resides, so a certified copy must also go to the Registrar of Lands for the district in which the Tangalle land is situated. It confirms that the Ordinance already anticipates a notary attesting a deed about land outside his own district.
provisions.temporal_note: Consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against rule (29). In force at October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: means any written power or authority other than that given to an attorney at law for the purpose of appearing as an attorney at law on behalf of such person, given by one person to another, to represent him, to perform any work, do any act, or carry on any trade or business, and - (a) if it is executed in Sri Lanka, executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public
provisions.why_relevant: Definition of a power of attorney. The alternative route turns on this defined term: the person duly authorised under the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance must hold an instrument answering this definition, which itself has to be executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary.
provisions.temporal_note: Section 2 reflects amendments up to the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024; in force before October 2025.
provisions.verifier_note: The dropped lemma is resolved from the corpus row's defined_terms, which lists attorney, power of attorney and Registrar General in the order in which the three limbs appear, so the quoted words are the definition of power of attorney.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (2) If a power of attorney specified in subsection (1) is executed in Sri Lanka, it shall - (a) be duly attested by a notary public in accordance with the Notaries Ordinance (Chapter 107) and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance;
provisions.why_relevant: A power of attorney used for a transaction within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, which a deed of partition of land is, must satisfy this section: notarial attestation, a description of the land with metes and bounds and extent, the registration reference, the grantor's thumb impression and identity copies. It sets the conditions the Tangalle party's authority would have to meet.
provisions.temporal_note: Section 3A was inserted in 2022 (Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022) and is recorded in the corpus as in force from 2022, before October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: shall submit his power of attorney for registration, if it is executed in Sri Lanka within one month and if it is executed outside Sri Lanka within three months, from the date of execution of the power of attorney
provisions.why_relevant: Registration of the power of attorney with the Registrar-General within one month of execution. Relevant to whether the attorney route can be completed in time and in order.
provisions.temporal_note: Section 3 reflects the 2022 amendment; in force before October 2025.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed but the subsection is section 3(1)(b), not section 3(1) as a whole; paragraph (a) of the same subsection carries the general obligation to register.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (b) be satisfied that the power of attorney has not been revoked or cancelled and shall state such fact in his attestation
provisions.why_relevant: If the Tangalle party signs through an attorney, the notary attesting the partition deed must check the registers and state in the attestation that the power is unrevoked. It is a step the answer has to name for the attorney route to be practicable advice.
provisions.temporal_note: Inserted in 2022; corpus records in force from 2022, before October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (30) If he attest any deed or instrument executed before him by means of an attorney, he shall preserve a true copy of the power of attorney with his protocol, and shall forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
provisions.why_relevant: The notarial record-keeping obligation that attaches when a party signs through an attorney, completing the attorney route.
provisions.temporal_note: Consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against rule (30). In force at October 2025.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (c) where a deed or instrument is signed by an attorney, such attorney shall submit to the notary an affidavit affirming that the Power of Attorney is genuine and in force and the grantor is alive when executing such deed or instrument;
provisions.why_relevant: A further condition on the attorney route added by recent amendment: the attorney must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine, in force and the grantor alive at execution.
provisions.temporal_note: This paragraph sits in the group inserted into section 31 by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and amended by No. 6 of 2024; in force before October 2025. The corpus text does not carry a rule number for this group, which follows rule (15); it is cited here as rule (15A)(c) and the numbering should be checked against the printed amendment.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed verbatim, but the corpus carries this paragraph in an unnumbered group immediately after rule (15) and gives it no rule number, so the citation rule (15A)(c) cannot be confirmed from the corpus and should be checked against the printed amending Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance
provisions.relevant_excerpt: be valid and effectual, so far as relates to the execution thereof, if the same be signed by the party making the same or by some person lawfully authorized by him, and by two or more witnesses present at the same time, in the presence of some District Judge or Commissioner of a Court of Requests* for the district in which the party making such writing, deed, or instrument, or the person signing the same as such attorney, resides
provisions.why_relevant: A third statutory route that meets the facts squarely: a deed which section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance would otherwise require to be notarially executed is valid if executed before the District Judge for the district in which that party resides. The Tangalle co-owner resides in that district, so she could execute there without a notary and without anyone travelling to Colombo.
provisions.temporal_note: The Ordinance dates from 1852 and the corpus records no amendment or repeal of section 2. The reference to a Commissioner of a Court of Requests is marked in the corpus text as an obsolete office; only the District Judge limb is relied on. Whether the section remains in practical use at October 2025 could not be confirmed from this corpus.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed and the corpus records no repeal, but the section is keyed to a District Judge or Commissioner of a Court of Requests, an office abolished by court-structure legislation outside this corpus, and the corpus does not show whether one party of four may execute before the officer while the others execute before notaries, so the availability of this route at October 2025 cannot be resolved here.

provisions.formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance
provisions.relevant_excerpt: nor until the same shall have been read over and explained to the party making the same, and to the witnesses thereto, by or in the presence of such Judge, Commissioner, or Justice as aforesaid, nor unless the same, and the duplicate thereof, shall be legibly written or engrossed, without erasures therein
provisions.why_relevant: Sets the conditions the officer must satisfy before certifying: proper stamping, reading over and explanation, legible engrossment without erasures, and identification of the party. It is what the third route costs in practice.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1852 section; no amendment event recorded. Availability depends on the same question raised for section 2.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed; availability depends entirely on PROV-M020-017, which is unresolved.

provisions.formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance

provisions.temporal_note: Original 1852 section; no amendment event recorded.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording confirmed; availability depends entirely on PROV-M020-017, which is unresolved. Section 5, which prescribes the form of the officer's certificate, was not mapped.

provisions.why_relevant: Gives the consequence of the Colombo notary going to Tangalle to attest in breach of rule (22): an offence punishable by a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees, besides civil liability. It shows the territorial bar is not merely directory.
provisions.temporal_note: Penalty amounts in section 34 reflect later amendment; the consolidated text relied on was in force at October 2025.
provisions.verifier_note: Confirmed: rule (22) is not listed in section 34(1)(a) or (b), so a breach of it falls under the residual paragraph (c).

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every notary shall be bound to have his office within the area specified in his warrant
provisions.why_relevant: Background on how tightly the Ordinance ties a notary to his area; it explains the scheme in which rule (22) sits but is not needed for any step of the reasoning.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1907 section; no amendment event recorded.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: No instrument shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the failure of any notary to observe any provision of any rule set out in section 31 in respect of any matter of form
provisions.why_relevant: Background: a breach of a section 31 rule in a matter of form does not by itself invalidate the instrument, but the proviso preserves invalidity under other written law, so it gives no comfort against a breach of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1907 section; no amendment event recorded.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question asks how the four parties can sign a deed of partition when the notary is licensed for Colombo and one party cannot travel there. Every step of the answer is supplied by statute: section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance for the form of a deed affecting land, rule (22) of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance read with section 3 for the territorial limit of the warrant, rule (25) of section 31 and section 32(2) for execution before more than one notary at different times and places, section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance with the Powers of Attorney Ordinance for signature by an authorised person, and section 2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance for execution before a District Judge. No judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed to state the available methods.

legal_issues.issue: Whether a notary whose warrant is limited to the Colombo judicial zone may attest the signature of a party who is in Tangalle, or attest a deed relating to land situated at Tangalle.

Whether a deed of partition affecting immovable property may validly be signed by its parties at different times and places, and before more than one notary, rather than by all four parties at one sitting.
Whether the party who cannot travel may instead sign through a duly authorised person under a power of attorney, and what conditions such a power and its use must satisfy.
Whether execution before the District Judge of the district in which the absent party resides is an available alternative to notarial execution.

questions.hop_count_basis: Four necessary linked steps across three enactments. Step one: the deed affects immovable property, so section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance requires signature by every executant, or by a duly authorised person, and the witnesses before a licensed notary, reinforced by rule (12) of section 31. Step two: section 3 of the Notaries Ordinance confines the warrant to a judicial zone, and rule (22) forbids attestation outside that area, so the Colombo notary cannot take the Tangalle signature in Tangalle. Step three: rule (25) and section 32(2) permit the same deed to be executed before more than one notary and at different times and places. Step four: the alternative routes each need their own enactment, the Powers of Attorney Ordinance definition in section 2 with section 3A(2) for the attorney route and section 2 of Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 for the District Judge route. Verifier: the hop count is unchanged at four. The provisions added on verification, rule (20), rule (25)(b) and (c), rule (3) and section 3C of the Powers of Attorney Ordinance, sit inside hops already counted and add no new reasoning step.

enrichment.original_background: There are 4 parties in a Deed of partition of a property in Tangalle to be executed before a Notary who has a license to Practise in Colombo. One party to the deed of partition resides in Tangalle and is unable to come to Colombo. However, the other three parties are residing in Colombo.
enrichment.enriched_background:
There are 4 parties in a Deed of partition of a property in Tangalle to be executed before a Notary who has a license to Practise in Colombo. One party to the deed of partition resides in Tangalle and is unable to come to Colombo. However, the other three parties are residing in Colombo.

The four parties are Ranjan Weerakoon, Malini Weerakoon, Suranga Weerakoon and Kanthi Weerakoon, the children of the late H. P. Weerakoon, who took the property in undivided one-fourth shares on his death in 2019. Ranjan, Malini and Suranga live at Kirula Road, Colombo 05, and Kanthi lives at the property itself.

The property is an allotment of residential land of thirty-two perches in extent called Muhudu Watta, bearing Assessment No. 118, Beliatta Road, Tangalle, within the Tangalle Urban Council limits in the Hambantota District. It carries a single dwelling house and a small coconut garden and is not a tea or rubber estate. Title is registered in Volume 214 Folio 63 of the Tangalle Land Registry, and the land is not subject to any mortgage or lease. The parties have agreed the four lots into which it is to be divided on a survey plan prepared in August 2025.

The Notary instructed is Mr. A. D. Jayasuriya, whose warrant authorises him to practise as a Notary in the Sinhala language within the Colombo judicial zone and whose office is at Ward Place, Colombo 07. Tangalle is not within that zone.

Kanthi Weerakoon is 78 years old, has been bedridden since a hip fracture in June 2025, and her physician has advised against any travel for at least six months. Mr. S. Kumarasiri is a Notary whose warrant authorises him to practise in the Sinhala language within the judicial zone that includes Tangalle; he practises from an office in Tangalle town and is willing to attend at Kanthi's residence. Kanthi is also willing, if it is more convenient, to authorise her nephew Nuwan Weerakoon of Colombo 05 to sign on her behalf; no such authority has yet been given. All four parties want the deed signed and completed during October 2025, and each of them holds a current national identity card.

added_facts.fact: The four parties are named as Ranjan, Malini, Suranga and Kanthi Weerakoon, the children of the late H. P. Weerakoon, who hold the property in undivided one-fourth shares acquired on his death in 2019; the first three live at Kirula Road, Colombo 05, and Kanthi lives at the property in Tangalle.
added_facts.reason: The question gives no party identities. Naming the four co-owners and their undivided shares makes it determinate that all four are executants of one deed of partition, without changing which statutory route is available.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the parties were not co-owners in undivided shares the instrument would not be a deed of partition and the execution analysis would be unchanged, so this fact fixes the scenario without shifting the outcome.

added_facts.fact: The property is an allotment of residential land of thirty-two perches called Muhudu Watta, Assessment No. 118, Beliatta Road, Tangalle, within the Tangalle Urban Council limits in the Hambantota District, registered in Volume 214 Folio 63 of the Tangalle Land Registry, carrying a dwelling house and a small coconut garden, unmortgaged and unleased, and not a tea or rubber estate.
added_facts.reason: The question says only that the property is in Tangalle. Fixing the district and land registry makes the deed one affecting immovable property in a district other than the notary's, which is what engages rule (29), and stating that it is not a tea or rubber estate keeps the Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act No. 2 of 1958 out of the analysis.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: Were the land a tea or rubber estate, partition by deed would need the consent of the Board under the fragmentation legislation and the answer would have to address that consent as well as execution. Were the land in the Colombo district, rule (29) would not apply and no separate certified copy would go to another land registry.

added_facts.fact: The Notary instructed, Mr. A. D. Jayasuriya, holds a warrant authorising him to practise as a Notary in the Sinhala language within the Colombo judicial zone, his office is at Ward Place, Colombo 07, and Tangalle is not within that zone.
added_facts.reason: The original says only that the notary has a licence to practise in Colombo. Stating the zone of the warrant is what makes the territorial prohibition operate, since the prohibition is expressed by reference to the area in which the notary is authorised to practise.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the notary's warrant covered the zone in which Tangalle lies, he could travel to the absent party and take her signature there, and the whole difficulty would disappear.

added_facts.fact: Kanthi Weerakoon is 78, has been bedridden since a hip fracture in June 2025, and has been medically advised against travel for at least six months.
added_facts.reason: The original states only that she is unable to come to Colombo. Making the inability durable rules out the simplest answer, that the parties wait until she can travel, and forces the analysis onto the alternative modes of execution.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If her inability were short term the parties could simply postpone her signature, subject only to the three month limit on completing a deed signed at different times.

added_facts.fact: Mr. S. Kumarasiri is a Notary whose warrant authorises him to practise in the Sinhala language within the judicial zone that includes Tangalle, he practises from an office in Tangalle town, and he is willing to attend at Kanthi Weerakoon's residence.
added_facts.reason: The multi-notary route needs a second notary who is authorised for the area where the absent party is. Without such a person the route is theoretical, and the question could not be answered on the facts as given.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If no notary authorised for that area were available, the parties would be left with the power of attorney route or execution before the District Judge.

added_facts.fact: Kanthi Weerakoon is willing, if it is more convenient, to authorise her nephew Nuwan Weerakoon of Colombo 05 to sign on her behalf, but no such authority has yet been given.

gold_answer_draft.issue: The issue is how the signatures of all four co-owners can lawfully be placed on a single deed of partition of land at Tangalle when the notary instructed holds a warrant limited to the Colombo judicial zone, three of the parties are in Colombo, and the fourth is in Tangalle and cannot travel. The sub-issues are whether the Colombo notary may attest in Tangalle, whether the parties may sign at different times and places, whether the absent party may sign through an authorised person, and whether execution before a public officer is an alternative.
gold_answer_draft.rule: A deed of partition affects immovable property, so Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a) governs its form: it must be in writing and signed by every executant, or by any person duly authorised by such executant, and by the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and attested by that notary. Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (12) states the same requirement as a duty of the notary. A notary's warrant runs only within the judicial zone in which he resides (Notaries Ordinance s.3(1), extended from division to zone by s.4A), and by s.31 rule (22) he shall not attest any deed in any area other than that in which he is authorised to practise; a breach is an offence carrying a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees besides civil liability (s.34(1)(c)), and s.33 does not save a breach of another written law. The Ordinance nevertheless allows a deed to be completed piecemeal. Section 32(2) applies where a deed to be executed by two or more parties is not signed by all of them at the same time and place, and s.31 rule (25) governs a deed executed or acknowledged before more than one notary: the notary who first attests complies with the whole of rule (20) and keeps the protocol, every other attesting notary complies with paragraphs (a) to (e) of rule (20), numbers the deed under rule (23) and keeps a certified copy as his protocol. By rule (28) the duplicate is transmitted by the notary who first attests, and by rule (29), the land lying in another district, a certified copy must also go to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which the land is situated. Rule (27)(c)(ii) means the deed should be completed within three months of the first signature. As an alternative, s.2(1)(a) of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance permits signature by a person duly authorised by the executant. Such authority must be a power of attorney within Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.2, executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary; because it is granted for a transaction within s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance it must also satisfy s.3A(2), namely notarial attestation in accordance with the Notaries Ordinance and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, a description of the land with metes and bounds and extent, the volume and folio of prior registration, the grantor's thumb impression and copies of identity documents. It must be registered with the Registrar-General within one month of execution (s.3), the attesting notary must satisfy himself that it has not been revoked or cancelled and say so in the attestation (s.3B(1)(b)), the attorney must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine, in force and the grantor alive (Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (15A)(c)), and the notary must keep a true copy with his protocol and forward a copy with the duplicate (rule (30)). A third route lies outside the Notaries Ordinance: by s.2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance a deed which s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance would otherwise require to be notarially executed is valid if signed by the party, or by a person lawfully authorised by him, and by two or more witnesses present at the same time, before the District Judge for the district in which that party resides, and certified by that officer, subject to the conditions in s.4 and the duplicate and registration requirements of s.3.
gold_answer_draft.application: The deed is fully engrossed before any signature is taken, so signing may begin. Ranjan, Malini and Suranga are in Colombo and can attend Mr. Jayasuriya's office; they and two witnesses sign there in his presence and in the presence of one another, and he attests under s.31 rule (20), which satisfies Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a) and s.31 rule (12) as to those three executants. Kanthi cannot come to Colombo and, being bedridden on medical advice for six months, cannot be waited for. Mr. Jayasuriya cannot go to her, because his warrant is confined to the Colombo judicial zone and Tangalle is outside it, so attesting there would breach s.31 rule (22) and expose him to the penalty in s.34(1)(c). Three lawful courses remain. First, the same deed may be taken to Tangalle and Kanthi's signature obtained at her residence before Mr. Kumarasiri, whose warrant covers that zone, with two witnesses signing in his presence and in the presence of one another; s.32(2) accommodates the different time and place, and s.31 rule (25) tells each notary what to do, Mr. Jayasuriya as the first attesting notary complying with the whole of rule (20) and keeping the protocol and Mr. Kumarasiri complying with paragraphs (a) to (e), numbering the deed in his own series and keeping a certified copy as his protocol. Mr. Jayasuriya then transmits the duplicate under rule (28), and because the land is in the Hambantota District a certified copy goes to that district's Registrar of Lands under rule (29). Second, Kanthi may grant her nephew Nuwan a power of attorney answering Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.2 and s.3A(2), which itself must be attested by a notary and can be attested where she is by a notary authorised for that area, register it with the Registrar-General within one month under s.3, whereupon Nuwan signs the partition deed in Colombo before Mr. Jayasuriya, who must verify under s.3B(1)(b) that the power stands unrevoked and state that in his attestation, take the attorney's affidavit under s.31 rule (15A)(c), and keep and forward copies of the power under rule (30). Third, Kanthi may execute the deed before the District Judge for the district in which she resides under s.2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance, with two witnesses present at the same time and the deed read over and explained and the other conditions of s.4 met, the duplicate then being transmitted for registration under s.3. On any of the three courses the parties should complete all signatures well within three months of the first, as rule (27)(c)(ii) contemplates, and they intend to finish within October 2025.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: All four parties can sign the deed of partition without the Colombo notary leaving his zone and without the Tangalle party travelling. The preferred course is for the three Colombo parties to sign before Mr. Jayasuriya in Colombo and for Kanthi to sign the same deed before Mr. Kumarasiri at Tangalle, the deed being executed before two notaries at different times and places under Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (25) and s.32(2), with Mr. Jayasuriya as first attesting notary keeping the protocol and transmitting the duplicate under rule (28) and sending a certified copy to the Registrar of Lands for the district in which the land lies under rule (29). Failing that, Kanthi may sign through an attorney under a power of attorney complying with Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.2, s.3A(2), s.3 and s.3B, used in accordance with Notaries Ordinance s.31 rules (15A)(c) and (30), or she may execute before the District Judge for her district under s.2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance. What the parties cannot do is have Mr. Jayasuriya attest her signature at Tangalle, or have her sign out of the presence of an attesting notary and witnesses, since either course would breach Notaries Ordinance s.31 rules (22) and (12) and, in the second case, deprive the deed of the form required by Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a). The availability of the District Judge route depends on Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 remaining unrepealed, which this analysis has not been able to confirm.

answer_claims.claim_text: A deed of partition affects immovable property, so it is of no force in law unless it is in writing and signed by every executant, or by a person duly authorised by the executant, and by the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and attested by that notary.
The notary may not attest a deed unless the executant and the witnesses signed it in his presence and in the presence of one another, and he signed in their presence.

A notary's warrant authorises him to practise only within the judicial zone in which he resides, and a warrant expressed for a judicial division is deemed to authorise practice in the corresponding judicial zone.

A notary must not authenticate or attest any deed in an area other than that in which he is authorised to practise, and a breach of that rule is an offence punishable by a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees in addition to any civil liability.

The Notaries Ordinance expressly contemplates a deed to be executed by two or more parties who do not all sign at the same time and place, and a deed executed or acknowledged before more than one notary, prescribing how the first attesting notary and every other attesting notary must attest, number and keep a protocol.

Where a deed is executed by two or more parties before more than one notary, the duplicate is transmitted by the notary who first attests, and where the land lies in a district other than that of the transmitting notary a certified copy must also be sent to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which the land is situated.

Where a deed is not signed by all parties within three months of the date on which it was first signed, the notary may be called on to deliver the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands, so staggered signing should be completed within that period.

A person duly authorised to sign for an executant must hold a power of attorney, which if executed in Sri Lanka must be executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary, and which, being granted for a transaction within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, must also be attested in accordance with the Notaries Ordinance and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and carry the prescribed land description, registration reference, thumb impression and identity copies.

A power of attorney must be submitted for registration with the Registrar-General within one month of execution where it is executed in Sri Lanka, the notary attesting the deed must satisfy himself that it has not been revoked or cancelled and state that in his attestation, the attorney must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine and in force and the grantor alive, and the notary must keep a true copy with his protocol and forward a like copy with the duplicate.

A deed which section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance would otherwise require to be notarially executed is also valid if signed by the party, or by a person lawfully authorised by him, and by two or more witnesses present at the same time, before the District Judge for the district in which that party resides and certified by that officer, subject to the reading over, stamping and legibility conditions and to execution in duplicate for transmission to the Registrar of Lands.

The three parties resident in Colombo can sign the engrossed deed with two witnesses at the Colombo notary's office, all present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and he can attest their signatures there.

The Colombo notary cannot travel to Tangalle to take the fourth party's signature, because Tangalle is outside the judicial zone covered by his warrant and attesting there would be a breach of the territorial rule.
Because the fourth party is bedridden for at least six months, the parties cannot simply postpone her signature until she can travel to Colombo, so an alternative mode of execution is necessary.

The same deed can be taken to Tangalle and signed there by the fourth party and two witnesses before a notary whose warrant covers that zone, the difference in time and place being provided for, with the Colombo notary as first attesting notary complying with the whole of the attestation rule and keeping the protocol and the Tangalle notary complying with paragraphs (a) to (e), numbering the deed in his own series and keeping a certified copy as his protocol.

On that course the Colombo notary transmits the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands of his own district and sends a certified copy to the Registrar of Lands for the district in which the Tangalle land is situated.

Alternatively the fourth party may grant a notarially attested power of attorney to her nephew in Colombo, taken at her residence by a notary authorised for that area and registered with the Registrar-General within one month, after which the nephew signs the deed in Colombo before the Colombo notary, who verifies that the power is unrevoked, takes the attorney's affidavit and keeps and forwards copies of the power.

As a further alternative the fourth party may execute the deed before the District Judge for the district in which she resides, with two witnesses present at the same time and the deed read over and explained, the duplicate then being transmitted for registration.

All four parties can therefore sign the same deed of partition, the three in Colombo before the Colombo notary and the fourth at Tangalle before a notary authorised for that zone, the deed being executed before two notaries at different times and places and completed within three months of the first signature.

If a second notary is not used, the fourth party may sign through an attorney under a power of attorney meeting the statutory conditions, or execute before the District Judge for her district, each of which produces a validly executed deed.

What the parties cannot lawfully do is have the Colombo notary attest the fourth party's signature at Tangalle, or have her sign away from an attesting notary and witnesses, and the saving for defects of form gives no protection where the form required by the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance is not met.

questions.block_reason: Two points need a lawyer before this becomes gold. First, PROV-M020-017 (Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 s.2), an indispensable provision behind the third route in the answer, is unresolved: the corpus records no repeal, but the section is keyed to a District Judge or Commissioner of a Court of Requests, an office abolished outside this corpus, and it does not address one party of four executing before the officer while the others execute before notaries. Second, CL-M020-Q01-001 assumes a deed of partition falls within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, which lists sales, transfers, assignments, mortgages and agreements affecting land but not partition, while Stamp Duty Act s.5(11) and Western Province Financial Statute s.106 treat a deed of partition as distinct from a transfer. The two-notary route and the attorney route are verified and the answer stands on them, so this is a review, not a rejection.
